sentences.text: Misc .
Appeal No. 3277 of 2022

National Insurance Company
 Versus
 Smt. Rekhabai And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Pankaj Kumar Jain, learned counsel for the respon
 Shri Vishwesh Palshikar, learned coun
 respondents/claimants- No.1 to 5.
 Order
With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

02. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Co. being aggrieved by the award dated 11.5.2022 passed in MACC No.64/2018 by the IInd Addl.
Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sarangpur, District Rajgarh (Biora) whereby a total sum of Rs.20,59,840/- has been awarded to the respondents No.1 to 5 / claimants by way of compensation.

entities.text:
IInd Addl.
Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sarangpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 03. Short facts of the case are that on 18.7.2018 deceased Parmanand was driving his tanker bearing registration No.M.P. 09 HG 9818 from Bavai to Bohpal at that time the driver of Eicher truck bearing registration No.M.P. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32183 2 MA-3277-2022 12 H 0395 came rashly and negligently and dashed with the tractor of Parmanand as a result of which deceased Parmanand received grievous injuries over his body and died on the spot.
The driver of the truck has also died in the said accident.
04. Thereafter the respondents No.1 to 5 / claimants filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 for award of compensation to them on account of his death.
The application was contested by appellant / Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation National Insurance Company vs Smt. Rekhabai on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13323765/
1 of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.20,59,840/- to the claimants.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs Smt. Rekhabai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However the liability of payment of compensation was fastened on the appellant / Insurance Company.

05. Learned counsel for the appellant / Insurance Co. submits that the claims tribunal has wrongly saddled the Insurance Company with liability to pay compensation for the reason that there was no driving license available with the owner, which has not been brought before the tribunal and the tribunal even after raising this issue specifically and filing of an application under Order 11 Rule 14 of the CPC for producing the said driving license has not recorded any clear finding on that issue and by observing incoherently in para 22 and 23 saddled the Insurance Co., with the liability to pay compensation as awarded in the case.
He submits that even if the affidavit is filed by the owner of the vehicle is seen then it would come to the fore he made an evasive averment in the affidavit.
He has stated that at the time of engaging the deceased/driver Krishnapal Singh, he has seen his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32183 3 MA-3277-2022 driving license.
However, the same is not available because the driver was keeping it with himself and after accident it was not found.
He submits that this averment in affidavit is not only evasive but also mischievous.

If the original driving license was being kept by the driver which is a natural phenomena, then the photocopy of the same should have been kept by the owner and in any case he could have mentioned the Office from where the driving license was issued believing the statement that the license was kept by the driver still some information about issuance of the same must have been kept by the owner with himself.
Apart from this he also points out that even the police at the time of investigation did not seize the driving license because of its unavailability at the spot of accident also.
He submits that it is a clear case of complete absence of driving license.
As such, the Insurance Company has wrongly been saddled with the liability of payment of compensation.

He in support of his submissions placed reliance on the order passed by this Court on 17/2/2024 in M.A.No.2206/2017.
06.

Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants submits that in the affidavit the owner has clearly averred that he had satisfied himself about the availability of the driving license at the time of engaging the driver.

Thus he has discharged his primary burden and it was the onus on the Insurance Co. to dispel the same which the Insurance Co. has failed to discharge and hence the claims tribunal has correctly saddled the Insurance Co. with liability to pay compensation.
Learned counsel in support of his submissions placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of Nirmala Khotari V/s.
United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Union reported as NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32183 4 MA-3277-2022 2020 (4) MPLJ 250 .

Apart from this he also submits that even in case there is doubt on the existence of driving license then also in light of National Insurance Co. Ltd V/s. Swarn Singh & Ors. 2004 ACJ 1 pay and recover should be directed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
07. Learned counsel for the respondent No.8 has expressed his inability to the dispute by stating that no liability has been imposed upon the Insurance Company / respondent No.8.
08.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

National Insurance Company vs Smt. Rekhabai on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13323765/
2 09.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs Smt. Rekhabai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 22 and 23 it is clear that there was complete absence of any material so as to establish existence of the driving license whereas only one document is available on record of the claims tribunal ie., affidavit of the owner of the insured vehicle in which he has stated in para 3 that at the time of engaging the deceased driver Krishnapal Singh Tomar he has seen his driving license and after satisfaction he engaged him.

However in the entire affidavit the particulars or any kind of details of the driving license ie., from which RTO Office it was issued and which is the concerned District from where the verification of the existence of driving license can be done was mentioned.
Though it has been stated in the affidavit that the original driving license was kept by the driver.
However, he has not stated that for what reasons he did not keep the copy of the said license in his records.
In fact, if para 4 of the affidavit is seen then it by itself speaks for the unreliability of his statement.
In para 4 of the affidavit he submits that the deceased driver was carrying his license at the time of accident.
However where it has gone after accident he NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32183 5 MA-3277-2022 is not aware about the same.
The police has made seizure of the entire material from the spot of accident in which everything except driving license was found.
As such, the affidavit of the owner is not reliable.
Secondly there are no findings on this issue by the claims tribunal in the impugned award.
Para 22 and 23 are incoherent and superficial.
The tribunal should have recorded the clear findings about the existence of license.
10. In view of the above findings it is hereby held that at the time of accident the driver of the vehicle was not carrying a valid license.

11. This court while considering the similar issue in the case of Branch Manager Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd V/s. Smt. Aarti Ahirwar & Another passed in M.A.No.2206 of 2017 has held in para 16 as under :-
"16.

entities.text: Branch Manager Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd V/s. Smt. Aarti Ahirwar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned tribunal has framed issues No.3 and 4 regarding driving licence and breach of policy and the tribunal has given findings in negative concluding that burden was not discharged by the insurance company.

It is true that issues No. 3 and 4 regarding breach of policy is to be proved by the insurance company but firstly it is the duty of the owner and driver of the offending vehicle to produce the driving licence then the burden shifts on the insurance company to rebut that the driving licence produced in the case was not valid and effective on the date of incident.

Since there is no driving licence filed before the tribunal and before the investigating agency, hence appellant-insurance company has no source to verify the validity and effectiveness of the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In the case of Pappu & others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another (2018) 3 SCC 208, Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - mere production of a valid insurance certificate in respect of offending vehicle is not enough for owner to make insurance company liable to discharge liability arising from rash and negligent driving by driver of his vehicle.

entities.text: Pappu & others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another (2018) 3 SCC 208
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insurance company can be fastened with liability on basis of a valid insurance policy only after basic facts are pleaded and established by owner of offending vehicle that vehicle was not only duly insured but also that it was driven by an authorized person having a valid driving licence."

National Insurance Company vs Smt. Rekhabai on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13323765/
3 12.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs Smt. Rekhabai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case the primary burden has not been discharged by the owner by providing any kind of details about the driving license.

As NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32183 6 MA-3277-2022 regards the reliance placed by the learned counsel for the claimants on the judgment of Nirmala Kothari (supra) the facts of that case were different.
In the said case the driver produced driving license before the owner and made him believe that it was a genuine driving license which after accident found forged before the claims tribunal.
In such circumstances, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the owner discharged his burdened by satisfying himself about the existence of a valid driving license.
13. In view of the above analysis and law it is hereby held that there was no valid license available at the time of accident before the claims tribunal.
14. In this view of the matter, the affidavit of the owner Punjab Singh cannot be relied.

However,
there is one more peculiar fact in the present case, the driver in question has also died in the same accident.
Considering this fact instead of remanding the matter back to the claims tribunal, this Court deems it proper to direct for pay and recover.

It is thus hereby directed that Insurance Company shall first pay the compensation to the claimants and then it may recover the same from owner of the vehicle.
15.
With the aforesaid, the appeal stands dismissed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
